title: Jaynes--Cummings dynamics of fermionic heteronuclear dimers in the Mott regime
authors: R. J. Lewis-Swan, K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract: We formulate and exactly solve a model for coherent association and dissociation of fermionic heteronuclear dimers in the deep-lattice Mott regime. Starting from the onsite three-component atom--molecule Hamiltonian, we show how the single-site model maps to the paradigmatic Jaynes--Cummings Hamiltonian from quantum optics. In this mapping, the fermionic molecular/free-atom sector forms an effective two-level system, while the bosonic atomic mode plays the role of the oscillator degree of freedom. We fix the conserved number of fermionic constituent atoms to one but allow an arbitrary conserved number $N$ of bosonic constituent atoms. The accessible doublet is then $|e,N-1\rangle\leftrightarrow|g,N\rangle$, and the coherent conversion coupling is bosonically enhanced to $χ\sqrt{N}$. Exact analytic expressions are derived for molecular dissociation, atom-pair association, mode populations, and boson--fermion correlation dynamics. The model provides a transparent matter-wave realization of Jaynes--Cummings physics in a heteronuclear Bose--Fermi system and an exactly solvable setting for understanding coherent atom--molecule conversion and bosonic enhancement in lattice systems.
summary: This theoretical paper models the coherent conversion between fermionic molecules and free atoms coupled to a bosonic matter wave field in an optical lattice Mott regime. By mapping the system dynamics onto the Jaynes--Cummings Hamiltonian, the authors derive exact solutions demonstrating bosonically enhanced coupling ($\propto \sqrt{N}$). This provides a powerful, solvable platform for studying atom-molecule chemistry using ultracold quantum gases.
main_problem: The paper addresses the coherent association and dissociation dynamics of fermionic heteronuclear dimers within a deep-lattice Mott regime.
main_result: It shows that the local dynamics map exactly to the Jaynes--Cummings Hamiltonian, yielding bosonically enhanced coupling ($\propto \sqrt{N}$) and providing exact analytic solutions for conversion probabilities.
method: The methodology involves deriving an onsite three-component atom--molecule Hamiltonian and restricting the analysis to a fixed-number sector that allows mapping to the standard Jaynes--Cummings form.
model_or_system: The system models fermionic heteronuclear dimers (molecules and free atoms) coupled to bosonic matter waves in optical lattices. The dynamics are analyzed by mapping the local Hamiltonian onto an effective two-level system interacting with a quantized oscillator field.
key_observables: Molecular dissociation probability ($P_N(t)$), atom-pair association probability, and site-dependent boson–fermion correlation functions ($g^{(2)}_{bf}$).
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), coupling strength ($\chi$), and the conserved number of bosonic atoms ($N$). The resonance condition is $\omega_m = \omega_f + \omega_b$.
main_assumptions: The model assumes an idealized limit where onsite interactions are treated perturbatively (renormalizing detuning) but do not alter the fundamental solvable structure or the coupling scaling ($\chi\sqrt{N}$).
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail derived analytical expressions for population dynamics and correlation functions based on the Rabi frequency $\Omega_N$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model (onsite Hamiltonian), derives the mapping to the Jaynes--Cummings form in specific fixed-number sectors ($N_{	ext{tot},f}=1$), solves the resulting dynamics analytically, and discusses extensions including onsite interactions.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct, exactly solvable matter-wave realization of fundamental quantum optics physics (Jaynes--Cummings) using ultracold atoms in optical lattices. The confirmation of bosonic enhancement ($\sqrt{N}$) is crucial for understanding coherent processes in many-body systems.
